source_metadata.source_type: rapid evidence review / clinical review (secondary source)

notes: The three SORT key recommendations intentionally overlap narrative recommendations but are retained because they are explicit, independently anchored recommendation statements with evidence ratings.

secondary_source_guardrail.note: This source is a rapid evidence review, not primary literature. Atoms describing underlying studies represent what this review reports and are tagged secondary_reported_result; they do not assert direct inspection of the cited primary studies.

schema_gaps: LiteratureAtom has no source-type field or dedicated secondary-review/recommendation atom kind.
Evidence grades such as SORT B/C have no dedicated field and are preserved as tags.
The model has no structured link from a secondary-reported result to its cited reference number/primary publication; this is preserved only in statement context/tags and the separate reference queue.

Diagnostic accuracy tables contain several metrics per test, while QuantitativeResult has one primary estimate; sensitivity is structured and the full reported metric profile is retained in original_result_text/canonical_statement.

A reported 20%-25% relapse range required a calculated midpoint (22.5%) for the mandatory QuantitativeResult.estimate field; the source range is preserved as an interval with interval_type=range and assertion_origin=calculated_from_reported_data.
extraction_limitations: Bibliographic references were not atomized as evidence.
Illustrative clinical photographs were reconciled in SEA but were not converted into evidence atoms because they are examples rather than independently quantified study assertions.
No external verification of guideline currency, FDA status, prices, or post-2021 evidence was performed because @VERIFY was not activated.
